question.text: Portfolio return 10.5%, risk-free 5.5%, beta 1. Treynor ratio:

explanation.text: The Logic: Treynor ratio = (Rp − Rf) / beta = (10.5% − 5.5%) / 1 = 5%, which expressed as a decimal is 0.05. This matches the worked example on p.150. The Trap: 0.01, 0.025, and 0.10 all misapply the formula — either by dropping the risk-free rate, halving the spread, or doubling it. The correct numerator is the 5 percentage-point excess return, and dividing by a beta of 1 leaves it unchanged. Note: Distributor-style pro-tip and cross-exam framing removed; explanation cleaned to neutral source-based wording from p.150.
